---
title: "What a cell shows"
description: "Read the status line and timer of an R cell, know the time limit, cancel a cell, and understand the 'From the book' line."
---

An **R cell** is a box in a note with R code in it. This page explains what the cell tells you while the code runs and after it has finished.

## While a cell runs {#status-line}

The top of the cell has one status line. It says what is happening right now. Most lines also show a timer, in minutes and seconds.

<!-- screenshot: cell-status-line — an R cell while it runs, with the status line "Running · 0:42 of 10:00" and the Cancel button; highlight the status line -->

| The cell says | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **Copying your files to the note…** | The files you added are being put where R can read them. | Wait. |
| **Waiting for a free R server (all are busy)… 0:12** | Other people are using all the R servers. Your cell is in the queue. | Wait. It starts by itself when a server is free. |
| **Starting R for this note (a first start can take 2 minutes)… 0:18** | The note is getting its own R. This happens the first time you run something in a note, and when you come back after a break. | Wait. Later cells in the same note start much faster. |
| **Waiting for the previous cell to finish…** | A note runs one cell at a time. An earlier cell is still running. | Wait, or cancel the earlier cell. |
| **Starting R…** | R is starting. | Wait. |
| **Restoring your saved session…** | R is loading the tables and results that the note saved earlier. | Wait. |
| **Running · 0:42 of 10:00** | R is running your code. The first time is how long it has run. The second is the [time limit](#time-limit). | Wait, or [cancel](#cancel) if you do not want the result. |
| **Cancelling…** | You asked the cell to stop. It is stopping. | Wait a moment. |
| **Interrupted by a server restart. Run the cell again.** | OmicsBase was restarted while your cell was waiting or running. The cell did not finish. | Run the cell again, or ask the agent to. |

### Output appears while the cell runs {#live-output}

The text that R prints shows up under the code while the cell runs. The box shows the last lines and scrolls as new lines come.

A long step that prints nothing until it is done shows its text when it ends.

## The time limit {#time-limit}

A cell can use **10 minutes of R time**.

- The clock starts when R starts running the code. That is when the cell says **Running**.
- Waiting does not count. Waiting for a free R server, starting R and restoring your session use none of the 10 minutes.
- The limit is the same for cells you run and cells the agent runs.

When the 10 minutes are over, the cell stops and says:

> Stopped after 10:00. R was restarted, so objects made since the session was last saved are gone. Run the earlier cells again to recreate them.

See [After a timeout or a cancel](#after-stop) for what that means.

If a step needs more than 10 minutes, ask the agent to split it into smaller steps or to use a smaller part of the data. For long jobs, use [Reports on Roihu](reports-roihu.qmd).

## Cancel a cell {#cancel}

1. Click the square button on the cell (**Cancel execution**).
   You can do this as soon as the cell has started, also while it waits, and also for cells the agent runs.
2. The cell says **Cancelling…**
3. The cell stops and says:

   > Cancelled. R was restarted, so objects made since the session was last saved are gone. Run the earlier cells again to recreate them.

## After a timeout or a cancel {#after-stop}

To stop a cell, OmicsBase restarts the note's R. It saves the note's R objects from time to time, and after a restart R loads the saved objects again. Objects made after the last save are gone.

What to do:

1. Run the earlier cells again, from the top, with the green play button on each cell. Or ask the agent: `Run the earlier steps again.`
2. Then run the cell that was stopped, if you still want its result.

The restart clears only R's memory. The note, its code, its earlier output and your files are unchanged.

## The "From the book" line {#book-badge}

When a cell has finished without an error, it can show one small grey line at the bottom of its output.

<!-- screenshot: cell-book-badge — a finished R cell with the line "From the book · OMA › Alpha diversity" under its output; highlight the line and its arrow -->

### From the book · OMA › Alpha diversity {#from-the-book}

The analysis functions in this cell are also used in that section of a book, here the "Alpha diversity" section of OMA.

- Click the line to open that section on the book's web page.
- Click the arrow to see the other sections that use the same functions, one group per function, and the version of the book.

Use it to read how the book's authors use the method, and to check the cell against it.

::: {.callout-important}
## What the line does not mean

The line says only that the same functions appear in the book. It does not check:

- that the analysis is right for your data,
- that the arguments are right,
- that the steps are in the right order.

Read the section and judge the result yourself.
:::

### Not in the books: LimROTS() {#not-in-the-books}

This line names analysis functions in the cell that none of the indexed books uses. In this example it is `LimROTS()`.

The cell ran without error. The books do not cover the method, so check it in its help page or paper, or ask the agent why it chose it.

### No line at all {#no-badge}

A cell shows no line when there is nothing to say about it:

- it uses only base R, such as reading a file, making a table or drawing a plot,
- it uses only accessors, such as `assay()` or `colData()`,
- it uses a function that the cell itself defined. OmicsBase cannot see inside such a function, so it says nothing.

A cell that failed shows no line either.

### Which books are indexed {#indexed-books}

- **OMA**: Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis
- **OSCA**, **OSCA basic** and **OSCA advanced**: Orchestrating Single-Cell Analysis
- **OSTA**: Orchestrating Spatial Transcriptomics Analysis
- **scrapbook**: single-cell analysis with scrapper
- **R for Mass Spectrometry**
- **Metabonaut**: metabolomics
- **rnaseqGene**: the RNA-seq workflow, from reads to genes
- **MOFA2**: multi-omics factor analysis
- **tidyomics** and **tidy spatial**: tidy-style analysis of omics and spatial data

The Bioconductor books (OMA, OSCA, OSTA, the two OSCA parts, scrapbook, rnaseqGene, MOFA2) are their Bioconductor 3.23 release editions; the others are the versions on their own websites. Package help pages and vignettes do not count as "the book".
